# Hash-pinned build dependencies for the Windows installer.
#
# Generated, not hand-written:
#   pip download pyinstaller==6.11.1 --platform win_amd64 --python-version 312 \
#       --only-binary=:all: --dest <tmp>
#   pip download pefile pywin32-ctypes --platform win_amd64 ... --no-deps
#   sha256 each wheel
#
# WHY the second command exists: `pip --platform` selects wheel-compatibility
# TAGS but does not change environment-marker evaluation, so PyInstaller's
# Windows-only dependencies -- gated on sys_platform == 'win32' -- are silently
# dropped when resolving from Linux. Installing this file with --require-hashes on
# the runner would then fail on unhashed packages. They are pinned explicitly.
#
# Consumed by build-installer.yml as:
#   pip install --require-hashes -r .github/requirements-windows.txt
# --require-hashes makes EVERY requirement mandatory-pinned, so adding a package
# without a hash fails the build rather than silently widening the trust boundary.
#
# To refresh: re-run the commands above and replace this file wholesale.

altgraph==0.17.5 \
    --hash=sha256:f3a22400bce1b0c701683820ac4f3b159cd301acab067c51c653e06961600597
packaging==26.3 \
    --hash=sha256:d7193f7c8e4e93f444fde0262bf90af30e16fa0ad0ad44cb553c87339b23cd1c
# NOT 2024.8.26: PyInstaller pins `pefile != 2024.8.26` (that release has a
# severe performance regression in its binary parsing), so the newest version
# its resolver accepts is 2023.2.7. Both the wheel and sdist hashes are listed;
# pip uses the wheel.
